html: † I. סִין n.pr.loc. Sin, i.e. Pelusium, E. frontier city of Egypt (Egyptian ʾImt = clay, of which סין is transl. (cf. Aramaic סְיָן clay), according to SteindorffBAS i. 599, who cp. Πηλούσιον (πηλός = dirt, mud), cf. BrugschDict. Géogr. 1081 ff.);—Ez 30:15 (𝔊 Σαιν acc.), + v 16, but here Co Toy read plausibly סון, i.e. סְוָן = Syene (v. [סְוָן], סְוֵנֵה), 𝔊 Συηνη.—On Pelusium v. Bd.Egyptian 4 (1898), 169.
